explanation.question_quote: Physical exam reveals a high-pitched, harsh, holosystolic murmur that is best heard at the lower left sternal border. No cyanosis is observed.
explanation.sentence: The child has exertional breathlessness and a harsh holosystolic murmur at the lower left sternal border, without cyanosis.
A holosystolic murmur best heard at the lower left sternal border is characteristic of a ventricular septal defect.
During systole, higher left ventricular pressure drives oxygenated blood through the defect into the right ventricle, producing a step-up in right ventricular oxygen tension.
Because the shunt does not introduce deoxygenated blood into the left ventricle, left ventricular and systemic arterial oxygen tensions remain normal.
